memos.scout:
The strongest honest case for buying ALON is limited, and I don't think it clears the bar.

What points toward real demand: the coin is classed ORGANIC with no airdrop dump seen, it's alive at 30.5 minutes, and the last 15 minutes show net buy flow of +36 SOL on 367 buyers, with a 1.6x return over that window. Top-3 holder concentration is 12.9%, and the top-5 buyer share at graduation is 17%, which is not obviously concentrated.

What argues against it, more heavily: the 30-minute return is -16% and the drawdown from the high is 70%, so the chart is a broken recovery, not momentum. The 15-minute sell volume (215 SOL) is nearly as large as the buy volume (251 SOL), and 392 sellers outnumber 367 buyers. Bundle share on the curve is 43%, and the first two minutes after graduation show a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.93 with a launch bot present, which is a pattern of coordinated early flipping. Pool depth is thin at about 80 SOL, so a round trip costs us most of the 1.4-5.1% fee and impact band, and our $20 ticket would be a small fraction of a pool this shallow.

Verdict: I see no case that demand will persist 30-60 minutes out. The last-15-minute uptick is a single bounce from a 70% drawd
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution after a sharp round-trip. The coin is down 70.5% from its 30-minute high despite a +162% last-15-minute return, and the 15-minute window shows sell SOL (215.4) well ahead of buy SOL (251.4) with 392 sellers versus 367 buyers, so the pump was absorbed by exits. Graduation came after 496s, with 43% bundle share and a 34% completer share, which points to coordinated early buyers now unloading. The first 2 minutes after graduation saw 526 SOL of buying but a 0.93 sell-to-buy ratio, which means supply was already cycling. Pool depth is only 79.6 SOL, so a $20 ticket plus a 1.4-5.1% round trip is a thin edge against a coin that has already dropped 70% from its high. Skip.
